extracted.intended_audience: Users of Singular/polymake libraries (computational algebra / algebraic geometry researchers and practitioners seeking programmatic routines for polytopes, fans, and related computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for the polymake.lib procedures (an interface from Singular to polymake/TOPCOM) describing usage, assumptions, returns, notes, and examples for computations with polytopes, fans, triangulations, and related lattice geometry routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: dualPolytope
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dualPolytope(p); p polytope. Return: polytope, the dual of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from library gfan.lib. Example shows creating a polytope via points and calling dualPolytope(p) to get AMBIENT_DIM, INEQUALITIES, EQUATIONS of the dual.

rubrics_metrics.name: newtonPolytope (gfan.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: newtonPolytope(f); f poly. Return: polytope, the convex hull of all exponent vectors of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from gfan.lib. Example: construct polynomial f=x+y+z; call newtonPolytope(f) and inspect AMBIENT_DIM, INEQUALITIES, EQUATIONS of the resulting polytope.

rubrics_metrics.name: vertices
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vertices(p); p polytope. Return: bigintmat, the vertices of p modulo its lineality space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from gfan.lib. Example demonstrates polytopeViaPoints and vertices(p) returning vertex coordinates (modulo lineality).

rubrics_metrics.name: polymakePolytope
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: polymakePolytope(points); points intmat. Return: list L with four entries: L[1] integer matrix whose rows are coordinates of vertices of the polytope; L[2] dimension of the polytope; L[3] adjacency list describing which vertices are connected; L[4] bigintmat whose rows multiplied by (1,var(1),...,var(nvar)) give linear equations describing the affine hull of the polytope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls polymake for vertex, dimension, and facet information; requires polymake installed and works only on LINUX in this library. Note: indexing convention differs from polymake (this library indexes vertices starting at 1). Example shows how to call and interpret np[1]..np[4].

rubrics_metrics.name: newtonPolytopeP
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: newtonPolytopeP(f); f poly. Return: list L with four entries: L[1] integer matrix of vertices of the Newton polytope of f; L[2] dimension; L[3] adjacency info (which vertices connect to which); L[4] bigintmat giving a linear system for the affine hull of the Newton polytope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls polymake; only works if polymake is installed. Note: by modifying the first column of L[4] one can move the affine hull to the origin to obtain equations needed for polymake when computing the normal fan. Examples show interpreting np[1]..np[4] and dimension behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: newtonPolytopeLP
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: newtonPolytopeLP(f); f poly. Return: list, the exponent vectors of the monomials occurring in f (i.e., the lattice points of the Newton polytope of f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows listing all lattice points (exponent vectors) of the Newton polytope returned in several indexed list entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: triangulations(polygon[,#]); polygon is a list of integer vectors representing affine coordinates of lattice points. Return: list where each entry corresponds to one triangulation; each triangulation is a list of integer vectors of size three, each vector specifying a triangle by indices of the input points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes all triangulations of the marked polytope (convex hull with markings). Requires TOPCOM (points2triangs) installed; optional argument 'regular' restricts to regular triangulations; optional 'keepfiles' preserves intermediate files. Note: indexing convention refers to polygon[i] (this library) whereas TOPCOM indexes from zero. Example demonstrates triangulations of unit square and their representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: secondaryPolytope
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: secondaryPolytope(polygon[,#]); polygon list. Return: list L such that L[1] is an intmat whose rows give affine coordinates of lattice points in the secondary polytope; L[2] is the list of corresponding triangulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers the marked polytope and computes lattice points of the secondary polytope corresponding to triangulations. If triangulations were already computed they can be passed as second argument to avoid recomputation. Requires TOPCOM (points2triangs) if triangulations need computing. Example shows extracting secpoly[1] and secpoly[2].

rubrics_metrics.name: cycleLength
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cycleLength(boundary,interior); boundary is a list of integer vectors describing a cycle in some convex lattice polygon ordered clockwise; interior is a lattice point in the interior. Return: string, the cycle length of the corresponding cycle in the dual tropical curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates boundary and interior inputs and returns a polynomial expression (e.g., -4*u11+u00+u02+u22+u20) representing the cycle length.

rubrics_metrics.name: splitPolygon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: splitPolygon(markings); markings is a list of integer vectors (lattice points) in the plane. Purpose: split the marked points into vertices, points on facets which are not vertices, and the interior points. Return: list L where L[1] lists vertices ordered clockwise (each entry [coord,position_in_markings]); L[2] lists points on each facet (with coordinates and original position); L[3] lists interior lattice points (with coordinates and original position).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows feeding a list of lattice points of a triangle with interior lattice points as markings and interpreting sp[1] (vertices), sp[2] (points on facets but not vertices), and sp[3] (interior points).

rubrics_metrics.name: eta
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: eta(triang,polygon); triang is a triangulation (list of integer vectors size 3), polygon has the format output by splitPolygon. Return: list of intvecs where each entry corresponds to a lattice point of the polygon and the intvec is the eta-vector describing that vertex of the Newton polytope discriminant whose dual cone in the Gröbner fan contains the cone of the secondary fan corresponding to the triangulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Gelfand, Kapranov, Zelevinski (GKZ) Ch. 10 for theory. Example demonstrates computing eta for a triangulation of a marked polygon and getting an eta-vector like 9,1,0,0,1,0,0,0,0,1.

rubrics_metrics.name: findOrientedBoundary
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: findOrientedBoundary(polygon); polygon is a list of integer vectors defining lattice points in the plane. Return: list l where l[1] is a list of integer vectors giving the boundary of the convex hull ordered clockwise, and l[2] is the list with redundant points removed (the vertices of the boundary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows calling the function on a point set and interpreting boundarypolygon[1] (points on boundary ordered clockwise) and boundarypolygon[2] (vertices).

rubrics_metrics.name: cyclePoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cyclePoints(triang,points,pt) where points is a list of integer vectors (marked polygon), triang is a triangulation (list of triples of indices), and pt is an index selecting a marked point. Purpose: consider the convex lattice polygon P spanned by points connected to points[pt] in triang and compute all marked points lying on the boundary of P ordered clockwise. Return: list of integer vectors on that boundary, or empty list if points[pt] is not a vertex in any triangle of triang.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows constructing points and triang and calling cyclePoints(triang,points,1) to obtain boundary lattice points around the selected marked point.

rubrics_metrics.name: latticeArea
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: latticeArea(polygon); polygon is a list of integer vectors in the plane. Return: int, the lattice area of the convex hull of polygon (i.e., twice the Euclidean area).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example computes latticeArea and returns an integer (e.g., 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: picksFormula
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: picksFormula(polygon); polygon list of integer vectors in the plane with convex hull C. Return: list L of three integers: L[1] lattice area of C (twice Euclidean area), L[2] number of lattice points on boundary of C, L[3] number of interior lattice points of C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The returned integers satisfy Pick's formula L[1] = L[2] + 2*L[3] - 2. Example demonstrates pick[1], pick[2], pick[3], and verifying the formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellipticNF
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ellipticNF(polygon); polygon is a list of integer vectors in the plane whose convex hull has precisely one interior lattice point (Newton polygon of an elliptic curve). Purpose: compute the normal form of the polygon with respect to unimodular affine transformations T = A*x + v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list L with L[1] vertices of normal form, L[2] matrix A of unimodular transformation, L[3] translation vector v, L[4] list giving images of original polygon points under T. Notes reference Poonen & Rodriguez-Villegas on the 16 normal forms. Example shows nf[1]..nf[4] and the matrix/vector transforming polygon points.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellipticNFDB
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ellipticNFDB(n[,#]); n integer between 1 and 16. Purpose: database of the 16 normal forms of planar polygons with precisely one interior point up to unimodular affine transformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list L with L[1] vertices of nth normal form, L[2] all lattice points of nth normal form, L[3] optional polynomial (only present if an optional parameter # is supplied and the basering has variables x and y). Example demonstrates retrieving nf[1] and nf[2].

rubrics_metrics.name: boundaryLatticePoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: boundaryLatticePoints(p); p polytope. Assume isBounded(p)==1. Return: intmat, all lattice points on the relative boundary of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows constructing a polytope via polytopeViaPoints(M) and obtaining a list of boundary lattice points. Requires polymake (and related packages) available.

rubrics_metrics.name: ehrhartPolynomialCoeff
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ehrhartPolynomialCoeff(p); p polytope. Assume isBounded(p)==1. Return: intvec (Ehrhart polynomial coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure calls external tools (e.g., latte, libnormaliz) via polymake and may produce warnings if outputs cannot be parsed. Example shows polymake warnings and eventual returned coefficients like 1,1,2,2. Note: documentation contains a copy-paste error in the Return description in the source; intended return is Ehrhart polynomial coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: fVectorP
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fVectorP(p); p polytope. Return: intvec, the f-vector of p (counts of faces of each dimension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates calling fVectorP and obtaining output like 6,12,8. Calls external packages (e.g., lrs) through polymake.

rubrics_metrics.name: facetVertexLatticeDistances
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: facetVertexLatticeDistances(p); p polytope. Return: intmat encoding lattice distances between vertices (columns) and facets (rows) of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows output matrix of lattice distances. Procedure uses polymake tooling under the hood.

rubrics_metrics.name: facetWidth
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: facetWidth(p); p polytope. Assume isBounded(p)==1. Return: int, maximal integral width over all facet normals (the facet width).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example returns an integer (e.g., 2). Requires polymake and related libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: facetWidths
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: facetWidths(p); p polytope. Assume isBounded(p)==1. Return: intvec, the integral widths for all facet normals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example returns a vector like 1,2,1,2. Calls polymake packages (PPL etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: gorensteinIndex
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gorensteinIndex(p); p polytope. Assume isGorenstein(p)==1. Return: int n such that n*p + v is reflexive for some translation v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the translation vector v can be computed with gorensteinVector(p). Example returns values like 2. Requires polymake support.

rubrics_metrics.name: gorensteinVector
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gorensteinVector(p); p polytope. Assume isGorenstein(p)==1. Return: intvec, a vector v such that n*p + v is reflexive for some factor n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factor n can be obtained via gorensteinIndex(p). Example returns a vector like 1,1,1.

rubrics_metrics.name: hStarVector
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: hStarVector(p); p polytope. Return: intvec, the h* (h-star) vector of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure may call external tools (latte, libnormaliz) via polymake and can emit warnings if parsing fails. Example shows returned vector like 1,3,11,1 and shows preceding polymake warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: hVector
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: hVector(p); p polytope. Return: intvec, the h-vector of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates calling hVector and getting results like 1,3,3,1; uses polymake packages (lrs, ppl).

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbertBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: hilbertBasis(c); c cone. Return: intmat, the Hilbert basis of c intersected with Z^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from polymake.lib. (Example appears in the source but is truncated in this chunk.)
